title: Using git submodules might make it simpler to update corpora
description:
Instead of manually updating the corpora, you might want to consider using git submodules.

On a local clone:

```sh
$ cd ~/devel/exp/forked
$ git clone https://github.com/gaborcsardi/rcorpora.git
$ cd rcorpora/inst
$ git rm -r corpora
$ git commit -a -m "removing manually updated corpora"
$ git submodule add https://github.com/dariusk/corpora
$ cd ..
$ git status
On branch x
Your branch is ahead of 'origin/x' by 1 commit.
  (use "git push" to publish your local commits)

Changes to be committed:
  (use "git restore --staged <file>..." to unstage)
	new file:   .gitmodules
	new file:   inst/corpora
$ git commit -a -m "added corpora as a submodule"
```

To update from the submodule remote, there are at least a couple of ways, the simplest is:

```sh
# from the root of the rcorpora local copy
$ git submodule update --remote inst/corpora
```

Just did something like this on a local fork, pushed it, and then to check that it works, installed `rcorpora` from that:

```r
> devtools::install_github("jmcastagnetto/rcorpora", ref = "using_submodules")
...
> library(rcorpora)
> length(corpora())
[1] 328
```

A good reference on working with submodules: https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Submodules

Will submit a PR with this change, just in case you want to use this idea.

title: corpora encoding
description:
**corpora**  returns wrong encoding.
I use R 3.3.1 under Windows x64 and **readLines** returns incorrect encoding.
call:

> rcorpora::corpora("words/stopwords/ru")

I think it would be great if encoding will be explicitly chosen inside **corpora** function:

> fromJSON(readLines(filename, warn = FALSE, **encoding = "UTF-8"**))

title: Updating datasets
description:
Hi @gaborcsardi, I'd like to use the `dog_names` dataset from `corpora` , but I noticed it's not yet available through rcorpora.  I'm not sure if you already have some systematic way of updating it or if I should just submit a PR for dog_names.json/all the newest corpora files.  Let me know what works best for you!

corpora animals page: https://github.com/dariusk/corpora/tree/master/data/animals
rcorpora animals page: https://github.com/gaborcsardi/rcorpora/tree/master/inst/corpora/data/animals

title: Add new datasets from https://github.com/dariusk/corpora to rcorpora
description:
@gaborcsardi Some new datasets have been added to https://github.com/dariusk/corpora. I wanted to be able to access them using `rcorpora` from R. Therefore, I copied the content of https://github.com/dariusk/corpora/tree/master/data into the data path, and verified the package was built correctly. I also re-ran `readme.Rmd` to reflect these changes.

The fork that contains these changes can be found: https://github.com/spsaaibi/rcorpora. Let me know if you would consider these in a PR for `rcorpora`.
